entries.name: Special education law
entries.definition: The body of law, such as the US Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, that sets the rights and services owed to students with disabilities.

entries.name: Special hazards suppression systems
entries.definition: Fire suppression systems that use gas, foam or other agents to protect high-value or high-risk areas, such as data centres and flammable-liquid stores.

entries.name: Special use airspace
entries.definition: Airspace in which flight activity is restricted or the activities of other users are limited, such as restricted, prohibited and military operations areas.

entries.name: Specimen processing
entries.definition: Receiving, labelling and preparing clinical specimens so they are ready for laboratory testing.

entries.name: Speech recognition software
entries.definition: Software that turns spoken words into text or commands, such as dictation programs and voice assistants.

entries.name: Speech therapy
entries.definition: Assessing and treating difficulties with speech, language, voice and swallowing, usually as a speech-language pathologist.

entries.name: Sphygmomanometer
entries.definition: A device with an inflatable cuff and a pressure gauge or display that is used to measure blood pressure.

entries.name: SpiderMonkey
entries.definition: Mozilla's JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, which runs scripts in the Firefox browser.

entries.name: Spine.js
entries.definition: A lightweight JavaScript framework for building web applications with the model-view-controller pattern.

entries.name: Spiritual care
entries.definition: Supporting the spiritual and emotional needs of patients, residents and their families, often as a chaplain or care worker.

entries.name: Splinting
entries.definition: Keeping an injured bone, joint or limb still by fixing it to a rigid support called a splint.

entries.name: Spock Framework
entries.definition: A testing and specification framework for Java and Groovy applications, in which tests are written as readable specifications.

entries.name: Sport governance
entries.definition: The structures, rules and decision-making by which sports organisations are directed, regulated and held accountable.

entries.name: Sports journalism
entries.definition: Reporting and writing about sports events, athletes and the business of sport for news outlets.

entries.name: Spray gun
entries.definition: A handheld tool that uses compressed air or pressure to spray paint or other liquid coatings onto a surface.

entries.name: Sprint retrospective
entries.definition: A meeting at the end of an agile sprint where the team looks back at how it worked and agrees what to improve next.

entries.name: SPServices
entries.definition: A jQuery library that wraps the SharePoint web services so that web pages can read and change SharePoint data.

entries.name: Sputter deposition
entries.definition: A thin-film coating technique in which ions knock atoms out of a target material so that they land on a surface as a film.

entries.name: Spyder
entries.definition: A free Python development environment aimed at scientific computing, with an editor, console and variable explorer.

entries.name: SQL-92
entries.definition: The 1992 revision of the SQL standard, which defined entry, intermediate and full levels of the database query language.

entries.name: SQL Server Analysis Services
entries.definition: The Microsoft SQL Server component for online analytical processing and tabular data models used in business intelligence.

entries.name: SQL Server Express LocalDB
entries.definition: A lightweight version of the SQL Server Express database engine for developers that starts on demand and needs no server setup.

entries.name: SQL Server Integration Services
entries.definition: Microsoft's tool in SQL Server for building data integration and extract, transform and load workflows.

entries.name: SQL tuning
entries.definition: Improving the speed and resource use of SQL queries, for example by rewriting them and adjusting indexes and statistics.

entries.name: SQuirreL SQL Client
entries.definition: A free, Java-based graphical program for browsing and querying SQL databases through JDBC.

entries.name: SSL/TLS security
entries.definition: Protecting network traffic with the SSL and TLS protocols, including managing certificates, keys and cipher settings.

entries.name: Stable Diffusion
entries.definition: An open text-to-image deep-learning model from Stability AI that generates pictures from written prompts.

entries.name: Stair and railing construction
entries.definition: Building and installing staircases and their handrails and balustrades.

entries.name: Stakeholder communication
entries.definition: Keeping the people affected by or interested in a project or organisation informed and engaged through suitable messages and channels.

entries.name: Standard ambient temperature and pressure
entries.definition: A set of reference conditions used in chemistry, usually 25 degrees Celsius (298.15 K) and a pressure of 1 bar.

entries.name: Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping
entries.definition: The International Maritime Organization convention that sets minimum standards for the training, certification and watchkeeping of seafarers.
variants: Standards of Training Certification and Watchkeeping

entries.name: Stanislavski's system
entries.definition: An approach to actor training developed by Konstantin Stanislavski, in which actors build a character from its goals, circumstances and inner life.

entries.name: Star and snowflake schemas
entries.definition: Two ways of laying out a data warehouse: a star schema joins one central fact table directly to dimension tables, while a snowflake schema splits the dimensions into further normalised tables.

entries.name: Statement on Auditing Standards No. 70
entries.definition: A former US auditing standard from the AICPA for examining and reporting on the controls of a service organisation, replaced by SSAE 16.

entries.name: Statements on Standards for Attestation Engagements
entries.definition: Auditing standards issued by the AICPA that govern attestation engagements, such as reports on the controls of a service organisation.
variants: Statement On Standards For Attestation Engagements (SSAE)

entries.name: Static HTML
entries.definition: Web pages written as fixed HTML files that a server sends as they are, without building them anew for each request.

entries.name: Statistical software
entries.definition: Programs for analysing data with statistical methods, such as R, SPSS, SAS and Stata.

entries.name: Statistics
entries.definition: Methods for reasoning from data and uncertainty.

entries.name: Sterile technique
entries.definition: Handling instruments, materials and patients in ways that keep them free from germs during medical procedures.

entries.name: STM32 Nucleo
entries.definition: A family of low-cost microcontroller development boards from STMicroelectronics built around STM32 chips.
